payload.name: PreserveSharedPartnerActivitiesInExtraction
payload.description: During extraction, when a speaker uses 'we' to describe an activity with a spouse/partner, generate a candidate memory that preserves the shared nature even if the partner is not named in the message.
content: During candidate extraction, treat first-person plural statements ('we', 'us', 'our') about activities as candidates for a shared-activity memory when the speaker has a known spouse/partner or the surrounding context identifies one.

Do not silently rewrite 'we' as the speaker alone: preserve the joint subject by using a relationship memory or an event memory whose content states the activity is shared with the spouse/partner, even if the partner's name is absent from the message.
Skip this rule for generic/impersonal 'we' and for statements where no specific companion is identifiable; leave first-person singular activity statements to the normal extraction path.

solves: Extraction sometimes drops or singularizes first-person plural statements, so memories of what a speaker and their spouse/partner do together are never created. Future questions asking about shared activities then have no supporting memory. This Skill applies when a speaker uses 'we' and the session context identifies the companion as a spouse/partner; it does not apply to generic or impersonal 'we' or to first-person singular statements about individual activities.
